turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Brennan, checks are done. Blood pressure was one thirty-eight over eighty-six, pulse seventy-eight, temperature thirty-six point seven. On in with you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. I can hardly get the shoe on at all. The toe is in bits.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sit down. Which toe?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Right big toe. Swelled up overnight, and it's very painful.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night. Went to bed grand, woke up with it throbbing. I don't know, doctor, it just came on.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Out of ten?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, an eight. Nine if I stand on it.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever or chills?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't think so. Well, I felt a bit hot, but I didn't take the—
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is it red?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye. Red and shiny.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other joint sore?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister's on biotin for her hair, she buys the tablets in the chemist and she says—
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not her. Your joints.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. No, just this one toe.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Skin broken? Pus?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any injury?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No injury.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Had this before?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): The same, a year back. Same toe. It settled itself after a few days.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Daily tablets?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a water tablet in the mornings, for the blood pressure. I don't take the biotin, that's my sister's.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which one, what dose?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Bendro-something. Two and a half milligrams, I think. Sure the box is at home.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the high blood pressure is ongoing. Alcohol?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Pints at the weekend. Yesterday evening, actually, I was going to—
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many pints?
[SEG0030] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, I'll not keep you, the printer ate his slip. The readings I gave you still stand.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Four or five, Friday and Saturday, none through the week. And well, actually, I did kick the leg of the chair yesterday evening. Slipped my mind.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain straight away after that?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not then. It came on in the night. I don't know if the kick is anything to do with it, doctor.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shoe and sock off. I'll look.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right big toe is red, swollen and warm, very tender on the joint. Skin intact, no pus. You can move it a fraction.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): The sheet touching it is desperate. That's nearly the worst.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): This looks like a gout flare in the big toe joint. Weekend beer and the water tablet fit it. The chair is not the main story. Working impression only.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Gout. My father had that. I don't know, doctor, are you sure?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. For pain, it's colchicine or an anti-inflammatory like naproxen. I'll not start naproxen with a water tablet and no recent kidney bloods.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): You pick, so. My stomach can be touchy with some tablets, I was going to say—
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Colchicine. Five hundred micrograms twice a day for three days. Stop it if you get diarrhoea.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. And if it's still bad?
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it's no better in three days, or if you get a fever, come straight back. Otherwise I'll see you in a week.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the foot up, ice if you can bear it, and ease off those weekend pints while this is hot.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll try with the pints. The ice, I don't know, it might be too sore.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood test today for uric acid, and kidney function while you're on that tablet.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the uric acid tell you for definite? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not on its own. It can be normal in a flare. We'll still do it.
[SEG0051] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can bring him for the bloods now. The chair is free.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do. Uric acid and a renal profile, today.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): And I keep taking the water tablet?
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Don't stop it. Same dose, mornings.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. The car park is the other worry, the ticket'll be up.
[SEG0056] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll book the week review at the desk. Mind the step on the way.
